pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-segments/data/research-allowlist.toml:10 The research pipeline's network-egress allowlist is a committed manifest, but its own header lets an operator replace it from the uncommitted local shadowrunr.toml, and ResearchAllowlist::from_domains accepts any list with no check that it is a subset of the built-in one, so egress can widen without a reviewed diff — even though line 9 says adding a domain is strictly owner-gated.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-segments/data/research-allowlist.toml:10 Deny-by-default holds (https-only, empty list refused), but 'replace' lets operator-local config widen egress. The standard says privilege grows only through a committed, reviewed manifest edit. Only shadowrunr.example.toml is tracked.

crates/shadowrunr-segments/src/cases.rs:291 Staged case files written by the research pipeline cross a process boundary. They load through typed serde into plain data structs, with no object-graph or code-constructing loader and no permissive flag.

crates/shadowrunr-segments/src/cases.rs:90 Here 'extraction' means extracting text from fetched HTML or plain text. The crate has no zip/tar/gzip unpacking; the 'zip' hits in the grep are only iterator .zip().

pairs.registryProposal: permission-manifest-scoping is written around platform capability manifests (windows, webviews, extensions). Application-level network-egress allowlists that live in data files and can be overridden by operator config are a common variant the technique does not name. It should state whether an operator override may only narrow the committed list (subset check) or may replace it, because 'narrow or replace' wording turns the committed manifest into a default rather than a bound.
